title: Decoded String at Index
summary: Given an encoded string, decode it by reading each character: write letters directly to the tape and repeat the entire tape according to digit instructions.
statement: Given an encoded string, decode it by reading each character: write letters directly to the tape and repeat the entire tape according to digit instructions. Return the k-th letter of the decoded string, considering a 1-indexed position.
constraints: Letters append normally; digit d repeats the entire current tape d times.
Return the one-indexed kth decoded character without constructing the huge tape.
reference_solution:
def decoded_character_at(s, k):
 size=0
 for char in s:size=size*int(char) if char.isdigit() else size+1
 for char in reversed(s):
  k%=size
  if k==0 and char.isalpha():return char
  size=size//int(char) if char.isdigit() else size-1

hints: Reverse traversal can undo repetition lengths without materializing repeated text.
Compute total decoded length, then walk backward reducing k modulo the current length.
At digit divide size; at letter return when k%size==0, else decrement size.
Repeated copies map a position to the same position in one copy, which modulo performs exactly.
